newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers flat, firmer tone seen on Japan VLCC.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers flat, firmer tone seen on Japan VLCC.

text.p: Middle East very large crude carriers (VLCCs) on voyages to Japan showed a firmer tone but most other sectors were flat in quiet Monday trade, brokers said.
"If you look at the VLCC list you will see there isn't a great amount of quality tonnage available, and the Japanese are very particular about quality," one broker said.
"The rate is about W70 with an upward trend."
Rates to Singapore were flat at W62.5/65 and W60 to the Red Sea.
In the Mideast/west market, the 275,000 tonne Ruhr Ore was fixed at W60 to Brazil for Petrobras.

The West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCC market also looked fairly strong, with the 261,500 tonne Stena Concept, recently given a Bureau Green Award Certificate, done at W72.5 for Sun. Brokers said the rate for 250,000 tonnes was creeping up towards the W70 mark from W67.5 on a shortage of tonnage.
In the ultra-large (ULCC) market the 350,000 tonne Marine Pacific was said done at W55 North Sea/U.S. Gulf for Shell and the Settebello was fixed at W68.75 Sidi Kreir/UKC for Exxon.
The inter-U.K./Cont and Mediterranean markets were quiet after the Med Aframax (80,000 tonne) sector briefly spiked up to W160 last week.
"Shell seems to have taken a lot of Sullom Voe production for July on VLCCs and 135,000 tonne ships, and that doesn't help, of course," said a Scandinavian Aframax broker.
Med and West Africa/USG Suezmaxes (130,000 tonners) were steady at W85/87.5.

Caribs/upcoast rates were also little changed, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes remaining at the W170 level where they were for most of last week. One broker said 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems were still at W190 but with a softer tone as there was plenty of tonnage around. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
